task.title: Handle an urgent email ticket: user reply and troubleshooting notes
task.brief: Read the ticket (below). In about 20 minutes write two short parts. (1) A reply to the user: polite, clear, what you need from them or what they can do right now, and when they will hear back. (2) Internal ticket notes: the priority you would set and why, your troubleshooting steps in the order you would try them (with what each step tells you), and one or two things to do afterwards so it doesn't happen again. A good answer is calm and helpful to the user, works from simple likely causes to harder ones, protects data and accounts, and uses the facts given.
task.material:
Ticket #48213 | Raised 9:12 am | Branch: Vijayawada | User: Anjali Menon, Accounts

"Outlook has not sent any mail since morning. Everything is stuck in Outbox. Today is the last day for GST filing and I must send the GSTR-1 workings to our CA by 1 pm. Please help urgently!!"

What the service desk can see:
- Anjali's mailbox is at 49.6 GB of a 50 GB limit.
- Webmail (Outlook on the web) login works for her from your side.
- Two other users in the same branch can send mail normally.
- Her Outbox has an email with a 38 MB Excel attachment at the top.
- Last night a password change was forced for all users; she changed hers at 8:50 am.
- Her laptop's antivirus shows up to date.
key_points: Sets high priority because of the 1 pm GST deadline, though only one user is affected
Offers an immediate workaround: send from webmail, or share the file via OneDrive/link instead of a large attachment
Spots the nearly full mailbox and helps archive or clear space
Spots the 38 MB attachment likely over the size limit and blocking the Outbox; move or delete it and resend smaller
Checks Outlook is using the new password (credential prompt, cached credentials) and is not in offline mode
Steps go from simple and likely to harder, noting what each step confirms
Reply is polite, gives a time for the next update, and avoids jargon
Prevention: mailbox size alerts or archiving policy, guidance on sending large files, password-change communication

rubric.label: Correct diagnosis
rubric.guide: 0 = misses the likely causes, 3 = finds one cause, 5 = links the full mailbox, large attachment and password change to sensible checks

rubric.label: Troubleshooting order
rubric.guide: 0 = random or risky steps, 3 = reasonable steps in a loose order, 5 = clear, logical steps from simple to complex with a fast workaround first

rubric.label: User communication
rubric.guide: 0 = rude, vague or full of jargon, 3 = polite but missing what to do or when, 5 = calm, clear actions and a time for the next update

rubric.label: Priority and prevention
rubric.guide: 0 = no priority or follow-up, 3 = priority set but weak reasons, 5 = justified priority and practical steps to prevent a repeat
